To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the decapod crustacea colonization during the Early Permian, in the Gouduni river section, was favoured by a semi-consolidation of sandstone-mud interbeds, which were deposited in a tide-wave influenced fluvial-marie interactive estuarine setting, and the colonization led to Glossifungitcs ichnofacies.

1) the Barakar Formation of the Talchir Coalfield, Odisha, is a fluvio-marine estuarine system; 2) the crustaceans of the Glossifungites Icnofacies colonized the semi-consolidated mudstone-sandstone heterolithic facie of the Barakarian succession; 3) the decapod crustacea, which colonized the semi consolidated mudstone-sandstones, were of marginal marine affinity;
the early Permian Barakarian sedimentary succession, eastern India, was deposited within a fluvio-marine transitional environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crustacean colonization and its impact on early Permian sedimentology in eastern peninsulaindia.
the ichnological signature of crustacean burrows, which is an important tool to understand the paleoenvironmental condition of the sedimentary rocks.

the recognition of a crustacean colonization in a semi-consolided substrate, and the interpretation of this ichnologic signature within the context of an early Permian fluvial-maritime transitional system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crustacean colonization was a result of the marine influence on the fluvial sedimentary system during the Early Permian in eastern India.
crustacean colonization in the Barakar Formation was a result of marine incursion into the estuarine environment.
the decapod crustacea colonization of the Barakarian sandstone-mudstones was due to the marine incursions during the early Permial in eastern Gondwanaland, India.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the crustacean colonization in the early Permian Barakaran Formation, eastern peninsular Gondwana, India is a result of a semi-consolidation of firmground under a tide-wave influenced marine incursion during prolonged phases of fluvial-marine interaction in an estuarine system.

the crustacean colonization of the semi-consolidated substratum was favoured by a combination of environmental factors, including the availability of suitable substrata, salinity changes, tidal influence, water depth, temperature, and food availability.
crustacean colonization in the early Permian of eastern India was not only confined to marginal marine environment but also extended to the fluvial system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Glossifungites ICF, previously considered to be restricted to marine settings, may have been developed in a fluvio-marine transitional environment during the early Permial in eastern peninsulain India.

crustacean colonization in the early Permian of eastern peninsular Gondwana was influenced by the marine influence on the fluvial system and the crustaceans were not restricted to marine settings alone.
crustacean colonization is a good indicator of marine incursion and the presence of crustacean ichnofacies is a good indicator for the presence of firmground.
